items.label: Current office
items.text: California State Controller; elected November 2022 and sworn in January 2, 2023. Also chairs the Franchise Tax Board. (sources: California State Controller's Office https://www.sco.ca.gov/eo_about_bio.html [search summary, primary]; California Franchise Tax Board https://www.ftb.ca.gov/about-ftb/bios/Controller.html [search summary, primary])

items.label: Previous offices
items.text: Member, San Francisco Board of Supervisors, including as board president and chair of its Budget and Finance Committee (years not stated in official bio seen); Member, California State Board of Equalization (District 2), elected November 2018, chair in 2019 and 2022, serving until 2022. (sources: California State Controller's Office https://www.sco.ca.gov/eo_about_bio.html [search summary, primary]; Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malia_Cohen [search summary, secondary])

items.label: Education
items.text: Bachelor's degree in political science, Fisk University; Master of Science in Public Policy and Management, Carnegie Mellon University Heinz College (2008). (sources: CalSTRS https://www.calstrs.com/malia-m-cohen [search summary, primary]; Carnegie Mellon University https://www.cmu.edu/engage/news-stories/alumni-hall-of-honor/bio-maliacohen [search summary, secondary])

items.label: Investment career
items.text: Founded Efficient Market Advisors, a San Diego investment firm, in 2004 and served as its CEO and chief investment officer; the firm was later acquired by Cantor Fitzgerald Investment Advisors, where he is listed as a senior managing director from 2017. (sources: iVoterGuide https://ivoterguide.com/candidate/91093/race/30575/election/1454 [search summary, secondary]; SCA Club https://financial.scaclub.org/node/99 [search summary, secondary]; LAist https://laist.com/news/politics/voter-guides/2026-election-california-general-state-controller [search summary, secondary])

items.label: Earlier career
items.text: Earlier held senior vice president roles at Linsco/Private Ledger, Dreyfus and ING Funds (formerly Pilgrim Funds), and worked at J. & W. Seligman & Co. from 1990 to 1996. One profile states he served as president of the board of the San Diego City Employees' Retirement System. (sources: SCA Club https://financial.scaclub.org/node/99 [search summary, secondary]; Podbay (WTFinance podcast bio) https://podbay.fm/p/wtfinance/e/1627570800 [search summary, secondary])

items.label: Education
items.text: B.A. in economics with honors, University of California, Santa Cruz (1988).
